answer: Each name stands on the ridge only after two established names vouch for it, and a seat may vouch for one newcomer per round, with voucher, fee and depth printed on the signal ledger. Exposure grows the further a vouched line sinks, locking its vote until the line climbs. A juniper stake matures three rounds later and is lost if the line stalls. An operator wanting k extra names must recruit k distinct gatekeeper pairs, paying a rising fee as free vouchers run dry, while clones vouching for each other lock mutual weight that cancels.
